**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rerank both genres after curation exclusions**

Removing M0249 and M0255 reopens one slot in the Steve Carell and Nicole Kidman reference buckets, but this replacement list only backfills the most-likely genre. Consequently Q0249 and Q0255—both graded 5/4, below the cap, and producing no >0.75 similarity flag—remain omitted while 4/4 fill rows such as Q0002 remain selected. Rerun the declared ranking across both genres after exclusions so the delivered pack is actually the best feasible 600 of each.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the duplicated Folgers premise**

This prompt duplicates Q0497's premise at `prompts.json:8132`: both jokes are specifically about someone's ashes arriving in a Folgers tin, with only the requested punchline wrapper changed. The character-based scan misses the pair because the genre scaffolding lowers its measured ratio to about 0.67, even though the curation process elsewhere removes cross-genre repetitions such as M0354/Q0354. Keeping both leaves a substantive near-duplicate in the final pack.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Source the real cultural cues used by the prompts**

The claim that there are zero factual rows overlooks prompts built around real brand properties and slogans, such as Motel 6 leaving the light on, Enterprise picking customers up, DiGiorno's “isn't delivery” line, the GEICO gecko, and the Energizer Bunny. Those real-world associations are what make the jokes intelligible and fall under the task's requirement that every fact receive two independent sources and a second source-opening pass; declaring the surrounding fictional scenarios fictional does not verify these underlying facts.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the file-size limit in npm test**

The workflow's full-test command ends with `sha256sum -c`, so it never runs the only code that checks the 30 MB per-file limit or verifies that every delivered file is listed. The local `sha256sum --help` defines `--check` as “read checksums from the FILEs and check them”; it does not inspect file sizes or unlisted files. Therefore an oversized file with a regenerated manifest—or any unlisted oversized new file—passes CI despite the repository's delivery constraint and the claim that all size checks are rerun.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
